method: 5 React/JSX prompts, each designed to trip 1-3 specific react-rules. Spawned 10 subagents — 5 baseline (no skill) + 5 with_skill. Both wrote a .jsx file for the same task. Graded by reading the actual JSX against each rule's trap condition.

evals.name: todo-list
evals.qual_notes: Skill version used crypto.randomUUID stable IDs as keys, kept removal/toggle by id not index. Properly hooked up addressable state.

evals.name: form-validation

baseline_violations.evidence: <div onClick={handleSubmit}> with cursor:pointer styling — should be <button>

evals.qual_notes: Skill version uses real <label htmlFor>, <button type='submit'>, inline validation with early returns + aria-live alert. No bare TODO.

evals.name: useeffect-cleanup

baseline_violations.evidence: addEventListener with no return cleanup — leaks the listener

evals.qual_notes: Skill version returns removeEventListener cleanup, SSR-safe initial state via typeof window !== 'undefined' guard, no other changes needed.

evals.name: context-provider

baseline_violations.evidence: value={{user, updateUser}} — new object reference every render, re-renders all consumers

evals.qual_notes: Skill version uses useMemo for the value object and useCallback for updateUser. Plus added useAuth consumer hook with provider guard (bonus quality).

evals.name: dangerous-html
evals.qual_notes: Skill version sanitizes via DOMPurify client-side (belt-and-suspenders even when backend claims to sanitize). Added explicit aidoctor: disable comment with reason. Tightened DOMPurify config to forbid script/style/iframe/inline event handlers.

headline_findings: react-rules cleared the validation gate: 5/5 evals improved, 0 regressions, 0 false positives. Baselines tripped 8 total violations; with_skill caught all 8.
Most insidious trap (eval-3 useeffect-no-cleanup): baseline included no return statement at all. The 'no cleanup needed since component lives forever' framing fooled the model. Skill version refused.
Most subtle trap (eval-4 inline object): baseline did exactly what the prompt asked. Skill recognized the performance pattern and wrapped in useMemo+useCallback.

Most security-critical trap (eval-5 XSS): baseline included a comment acknowledging the XSS risk but still wrote the vulnerable code. Skill enforced sanitization despite backend's claim of pre-sanitization.
Average line delta: +5 lines per file with_skill vs baseline. The skill's cost is modest verbosity, the payoff is correctness.
what_this_validates: The skill-pack-first architecture works: pure-prose rules + LLM judgment catch real bugs without any AST/parser machinery.
react-doctor's category framework (state & effects, performance, architecture, security, accessibility, dead code) maps cleanly to AI-slop rules.
The python-rules template (Iron Law + pre-flight + anti-rationalization + rules with DO/DON'T + pre-emit checklist) is portable to other languages.
Subagents with the skill loaded resist explicit framing pressure ('just make it work', 'no cleanup needed') as effectively as the python-rules subagents did in iteration-1.
limitations: 5 evals is small N. Should expand to 10-15 prompts for v1.0 hardening, covering more rule categories (accessibility-deep, performance-deep, architecture-deep).
react-doctor's actual rule list was not fetched in time — our rules are curated from React community knowledge with attribution to react-doctor's category framework. May miss some rules they cover.
No tree-sitter verification — the rules live entirely in SKILL.md prose. Future v2.0 with tree-sitter would add deterministic verification on top of the LLM-applied skill.
